references.text: God answers Israel's jealousy by making them jealous of a people who are not a people, a direct consequence of their provoking him with foreign gods
Judah did what was evil in the Lord's sight and provoked him to jealousy with their sins, more than their fathers had done
Baasha provoked the Lord to anger with the works of his hands, reflecting the theme of stirring up God's wrath
Israel aroused God's anger with their high places and provoked him to jealousy with their carved images
They offended the Lord with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them
Paul warns against provoking the Lord's jealousy by participating in idolatry, with direct reference to the Deuteronomy theme
Paul quotes from Deuteronomy 32 that God will make Israel jealous through a foolish people
